name: When is it time to replace rather than repair kitchen countertops?

mainEntity.name: When is it time to replace rather than repair kitchen countertops?

acceptedAnswer.text: You typically need to replace countertops when surfaces show severe cracking, deep staining, permanent burn marks, or structural sagging. If laminate counters are peeling, swelling from water penetration around the sink rim, or separating at seams, cosmetic repairs are rarely permanent solutions. Another common trigger is reconfiguring your kitchen layout, upgrading to an undermount sink, or installing larger appliances that require a different cutout footprint. Swapping worn counters restores hygiene, seals vulnerable cabinet framing against hidden water leaks, and updates the room's appearance.
acceptedAnswer.description: Counters need replacement when you experience severe cracking, water swelling around sink edges, peeling laminate, or when changing sink and appliance configurations.
